title: On a video, the tool bar holds the video tools and the rest wait under More
goal: A recording opens with the full picture-editing tool bar: marquee, crop, arrow, line, highlight, lens, pen, fill and more, sixteen buttons, with no Blade among them. The user's video design gives a video its own short set, Select, Blade, Title, Shape and Measure, with everything else one click away under More and every shortcut still working. Give a document with a timeline that tool bar.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html lines 384-416 (FLOATING TOOL BAR, D4 video inventory, #toolOvf More menu holding Title / Text, Shape, Measure when narrow) and docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md D4 'Video: Select . Blade/split . Title/Text . Shape . Measure . Hand . Zoom. (The timeline has its own Select/Blade in its local toolbar; they mirror the same tools.)'. The app has no Hand or Zoom tool anywhere (space-drag and the zoom slider do those jobs), so leave them out and say so in the audit rather than inventing two tools. Seen in /tmp/photonz-playtest/an-editing-session-walk/5-dissolve-sc.png (2026-09-24 04:44, Next defaults): sixteen buttons, no Blade; the timeline bar's Select/Blade is TimelineDock.swift toolButton('scissors') on editorState.isTimelineBlade. Machinery that exists: ToolBarLayout (PhotonzCore, families and groups, tested), the measured-fit overflow menu and overflowShortcuts in EditorView.swift ~1073, which today only appear when the bar runs out of room; docs/design/modes.md section 2 already says folding by GROUP into a permanently visible overflow, never one tool out of a group, and section 3 lists the way back (the key still arms it, with a quiet line). Why not a mode: the mode is one app-wide setting (swap-the-window-into-a-mode-from-a-chip-beside-t left rough), so switching every window into Video because one recording opened would fold other windows' panels; tie this to the document having time, as the timeline is. Build the fold in core so a-mode-is-written-down-so-pixel-art-can-be-added (which needs the same fold by mode) reuses it. trim-becomes-a-tool-and-the-recording-window-ret plans Trim in Crop's slot on a document with time; the mock's inventory has no Trim, so whichever lands second says in its log where Trim sits.
acceptance: With a recording open at Next defaults the tool bar shows Select, Blade, Title / Text, Shape and Measure in that order, then a More button holding every other tool, as video.html's floating tool bar draws it
Blade in the tool bar is the same tool as the timeline's own Blade: arming either lights both, B arms it, and a click on a clip cuts there
Every folded tool still answers its key: pressing it arms the tool and a quiet line says it is under More. A picture document with no time keeps today's bar exactly

Ships behind a new Next flag, on by default in Next; a walk at Next defaults opens a recording, reads the bar, arms a folded tool by its key and one from More. Audit written under queue/audits/ with a capture beside video.html's tool bar
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: measure pass 2026-09-24: 'every folded tool still answers its key' collides with premiere-s-timeline-keys-work-the-moment-a-recor, which wants J/K/L/I/O/M/B to mean the timeline's thing the moment a recording opens (today L on open picks the Line tool). Whichever lands second must honour the other.
